chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Whatever you speak to Allah in the obligatory prayer is fine, and it is not considered (detracting) speech."

key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak to Allah during obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that personal supplications (du'a) or other non-Quranic utterances directed to Allah during the obligatory prayer do not constitute 'kalam' that invalidates the ritual, thereby permitting flexibility in the prayer's structure. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the core of the prayer lies in the recitation of Al-Fatiha and the physical acts, while personal communication with the Divine is an accepted enhancement rather than a disruption. This ruling underscores the accessibility of the prayer for the individual believer, allowing for intimate dialogue with God without compromising the prayer's validity.
